records.abstract_pattern: Any company with multiple business segments can use this pattern to demonstrate resilience and improving financial health through a period of volatility. The key narrative device is showing how one segment's strong performance can compensate for another's weakness, proving the value of a diversified model and resulting in an improved consolidated financial trajectory.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: A bottom-line or profitability metric (e.g., Adj. EBITDA, Net Income, Operating Margin).

records.title: Uber today

records.core_message: Our platform uniquely serves two fundamental and complementary user needs: moving people ('Go') and delivering things ('Get'), creating a single, indispensable service for everyday life.

shows.specific_content: A four-panel collage illustrating the 'Go' (Mobility) and 'Get' (Delivery) pillars of the Uber platform. It includes the core 'Go -> <- Get' logo, mockups of advertisements showing use cases ('Go to your commute, Get your essentials'), and lists of example destinations ('Wall Street', 'The office') and delivered items ('Family pizza', 'CVS pharmacy'). The concept of 'Uber Pass' is shown as the unifying membership.
shows.data_points_shown: No quantitative data. Shows qualitative examples of 'Go' use cases (destinations like Wall Street, Home, JFK) and 'Get' use cases (items like chocolate cake, CVS pharmacy, IKEA assembly).

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern establishes a company's value proposition by simplifying its offerings into two distinct but complementary categories. It uses a memorable, often verb-based, dichotomy (e.g., 'Go' vs. 'Get', 'Create' vs. 'Consume') to define the core user needs it serves. This framework demonstrates how separate product lines or services form a cohesive ecosystem, often unified by a single brand or subscription, creating a whole that is greater than the sum of its parts. Any company with a multi-sided platform or a portfolio of related products can use this to articulate its overarching strategy and synergy.
works_for: Our platform helps you both find work and manage your finances.
We help you both learn new skills and apply them to get a job.
Our software lets you design your product and then sell it online.
We connect you with entertainment to watch at home and experiences to enjoy out.
Use our tools to build your app and our cloud to run it.
We provide the hardware for your smart home and the services that run on it.
Our marketplace lets you buy from creators and sell your own creations.

variable_elements.primary_metric: First core user action/verb (e.g., 'Go', 'Create', 'Learn')
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Second, complementary user action/verb (e.g., 'Get', 'Consume', 'Apply')
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison of two complementary parts of the same business ecosystem.

must_have: A clear definition of at least two distinct but related product lines or service categories
Example use cases for each category
A unifying concept (e.g., a brand, a subscription, a single app)
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a clear conceptual dichotomy. The business must have at least two major pillars that can be framed as complementary.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: Not data-driven. Requires a strong conceptual framework and brand messaging. At least 5-10 examples for each side of the dichotomy.

ideal_for: Explaining the synergy between two or more major business units.
Introducing a new, unified brand identity or subscription that spans multiple products.

Despite a seasonal dip in sales, our contribution margin per order has increased due to supply chain optimizations.
We maintained positive cash flow during the industry downturn by aggressively managing operating expenses.
Our user acquisition cost is decreasing while our customer lifetime value remains stable, proving marketing efficiency.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A top-line volume or revenue metric (e.g., Gross Bookings, GMV, Revenue, Units Sold).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A profitability or efficiency metric (e.g., Adjusted EBITDA, Contribution Margin, Gross Margin, Operating Margin).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time, showing performance through a period of volatility.

Showing that profitability is improving independent of top-line growth.

Justifying a valuation based on efficiency and future profit potential, not just current growth.

When your business is in a pure hyper-growth phase and profitability is not yet a focus.
If you don't have enough historical data to show a clear trend through a volatile period.

records.core_message: Our business has become more resilient to external shocks; even as COVID cases resurged, the negative impact on our operations was significantly less severe than in the initial wave, showing a moderating effect.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern demonstrates resilience by correlating a key business metric with a recurring external shock over time. It shows that while the initial shock caused a severe negative impact, subsequent occurrences of the same shock had a much smaller, moderated effect on the business. This visual argument proves that the company, its customers, and the market have adapted, reducing volatility and de-risking the business against that specific headwind. Any company can use this to tell a story of 'weathering the storm' and emerging stronger and more adaptable.
works_for: Our supply chain is now resilient to port closures; subsequent shutdowns had minimal impact on our inventory levels.
Consumer spending on our platform has stabilized despite recent inflation spikes, unlike the initial shock.
Our user engagement is no longer as affected by competitor product launches as it was initially.
Regulatory changes in Europe had a smaller impact on our growth this year compared to the initial GDPR implementation.

Our churn rate barely moved during the latest market downturn, proving our product's essential nature.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A core business performance metric (e.g., trips, revenue, user activity, production output).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: An external, often negative, event or factor (e.g., COVID cases, inflation rate, supply chain disruption index).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Time-series showing multiple waves or instances of the external event.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time, comparing the impact of the same external event at different points in time.

must_have: Time-series data for a key internal business metric
Time-series data for a correlated external factor/event
Key dates of external events to use as annotations
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs an initial sharp negative correlation between the external factor and the internal metric, followed by a demonstrably weaker correlation during subsequent waves of the external factor.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: At least two 'waves' of the external event and the corresponding business metric data, likely spanning 12+ months.

ideal_for: When reassuring investors that a known, recurring external risk is now manageable.
To explain a dip in performance while simultaneously showing underlying strength and adaptation.
When making the case that the business has 'weathered the storm' and is prepared for future volatility.
In a post-crisis narrative to show how the company has learned and become stronger.
To contextualize performance against a major macroeconomic or industry-specific headwind.
To prove that your customer base has become habituated to a new market reality.
avoid_when: If the impact of the external shock is not moderating, or is getting worse with each wave.
If you cannot clearly and honestly correlate your performance with the external factor.
If the story is too complex to be explained by a single external factor.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key performance indicator showing recovery (e.g., Gross Bookings, Revenue, User Activity, Production Volume).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Point-in-time snapshot (e.g., a specific month) compared to the same point in the previous year (YoY).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison across multiple internal segments (e.g., geographic markets, product lines, customer cohorts).

must_have: Time-series data for a key metric (e.g., revenue, bookings, users)

A clear 'before' period to compare against (e.g., previous year)

ideal_for: When you need to convince investors you're recovering from a major external shock (like a pandemic, recession, or regulatory change).
To show positive momentum during a business turnaround.
To highlight the resilience of your business model in the face of headwinds.
When you have uneven performance across markets and want to frame it positively.
To provide early evidence that a new strategy is starting to work.
When addressing concerns about a recent dip in performance.
avoid_when: When all your segments are still deeply in decline (e.g., all are below 50% recovery).
When you are showing consistent, uniform growth (a simple growth chart is better).
When you don't have a clear 'before' and 'after' event to frame the recovery against.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A demand-side user metric (e.g., Active Users, Customers, Subscribers).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A supply-side metric (e.g., Merchants, Creators, Listings, Partners).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time.

Time-series data for a related supply-side metric (e.g., active merchants/partners)

records.title: Significant progress made in 2020

records.core_message: Our investment strategy is working: mature markets are already profitable and still growing, while our investment markets are following the same playbook towards profitability at an even faster growth rate.

shows.specific_content: Two side-by-side bar charts comparing a 'Profitable markets' cohort and an 'Investment markets' cohort. records.abstract_pattern: This pattern proves a business model's long-term viability by segmenting the business into 'mature' and 'investment' cohorts. It first establishes a 'proof point' by showing that the mature cohort has achieved a key success metric (like profitability) while still maintaining growth. It then shows that the 'investment' cohort, while not yet at the goal, is on the same trajectory of improvement, often with even faster top-line growth. This 'proof point and pipeline' structure de-risks the investment in the emerging units by demonstrating a repeatable playbook for success.
works_for: Our enterprise customers are highly profitable, and our new SMB segment is following the same margin improvement path.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A profitability or efficiency metric (e.g., EBITDA margin, contribution margin, LTV/CAC)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A growth or scale metric (e.g., Revenue, Gross Bookings, User Count)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison between two or more internal segments defined by maturity, geography, or product line.

must_have: A logical way to segment the business into 'mature' and 'investment' cohorts
Time-series data for a key growth metric (e.g., revenue, bookings) for each cohort
Time-series data for a key profitability/efficiency metric (e.g., EBITDA margin, contribution margin) for each cohort
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: The 'mature' cohort must show positive/strong performance on the efficiency metric. The 'investment' cohort must show significant improvement on that same metric. Both cohorts should show strong growth.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: Two time periods (e.g., Q4'19 and Q4'20) for two segments on two different metrics.

ideal_for: Justifying continued investment in money-losing business units or markets.
Proving to investors that the overall business has a clear path to profitability.
Demonstrating a repeatable 'playbook' for entering and maturing new markets.
Answering concerns about high cash burn in a growth-stage company.
Showing that profitability and growth can be achieved simultaneously across different parts of the business.
avoid_when: Your 'investment' segments are not showing clear improvement in profitability.
You cannot logically segment your business into 'mature' and 'investment' cohorts.
Your 'mature' segments are not actually profitable or are in decline.

A key metric demonstrating traction for each initiative (e.g., early revenue, user count, partner adoption).
Visuals for each initiative (e.g., product screenshots, logos).

ideal_for: When a mature company needs to prove there's still significant growth ahead.
To justify a high valuation by showcasing an expanding Total Addressable Market (TAM).
To demonstrate the power of a platform business model to launch new ventures efficiently.
In an investor day presentation to highlight strategic priorities for the coming year.
To explain how an acquisition is being integrated to create new business lines.

When you want to highlight a strategic focus area that isn't yet a large part of the financials.
Signaling a move into a new, large, and potentially disruptive market.

records.title: Freight

records.core_message: The freight industry is undergoing a massive, technology-driven transformation towards outsourcing and consolidation, creating the perfect market conditions for a tech-forward platform like Uber Freight to win.

shows.specific_content: A three-part slide showing two major trends in the freight industry. On the left, a line chart shows the increasing penetration of 3rd-party logistics (3PL) over time. In the middle, a bar chart shows the market consolidating around the top 10 providers. On the right, a text box with a third-party quote concludes that technology platforms are poised to win in this changing environment.
shows.data_points_shown: Line Chart: 3PL Penetration of Total Freight Market grew from ~2% in 2000 to ~12% in 2018 (13% CAGR). Bar Chart: Market Share of Top 10 Providers grew from 25% in 2007 to an estimated 35% in 2020.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern establishes a compelling market opportunity by illustrating two distinct, long-term industry trends that are converging. It uses one chart to show a behavioral shift (e.g., adoption of a new model) and a second chart to show a structural shift (e.g., market consolidation). The argument is solidified with a third-party quote or data, framing the company's solution as the inevitable winner in this newly shaped market. It's a classic 'winds at our back' argument that builds conviction about the 'why now'.
works_for: The shift to remote work and increased cybersecurity threats creates a perfect storm for our zero-trust security platform.
The creator economy is exploding while creators are demanding better monetization, an opportunity our platform is built for.
Consumers are abandoning traditional cable for streaming, and the market is consolidating around a few platforms, positioning us to win.
The rise of e-commerce and the demand for sustainable packaging are converging, creating a massive opportunity for our biodegradable materials.
As enterprises move to the cloud, they are consolidating their software vendors, creating a winner-take-all market for our integrated suite.
Regulatory changes are forcing banks to digitize, and our compliance platform is the leading solution for this transition.
The gig economy is growing, and workers are demanding portable benefits, which our platform provides.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A metric showing a long-term behavioral or adoption shift (e.g., market penetration).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A metric showing a structural market change (e.g., market share concentration).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Market structure over time (past vs. present).

must_have: Time-series data showing a key market adoption trend (e.g., penetration rate)
Data comparing market structure at two different points in time (e.g., market share of top players)
A credible third-party source (report, analyst quote) to validate the trends
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs two clear, upward trends that logically connect to create a single narrative.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 5-10+ years for the time-series trend; 2 distinct time periods for the market structure comparison.

ideal_for: To answer the 'Why Now?' question in an investor pitch.
To establish a large, growing, and changing market opportunity.
When positioning your company as the leader of a fundamental industry transformation.
To build conviction that your success is driven by macro trends, not just internal execution.
In the opening section of a presentation to set the context for the entire story.
When you have strong third-party data that validates your view of the market.
avoid_when: Your market is mature and static.
You lack credible, third-party data to support your claims about market shifts.
You are creating a completely new category where historical trend data doesn't exist.

records.title: Technology is accelerating industry transformation

records.core_message: Our technology creates a powerful, self-reinforcing flywheel in our Freight business, where network growth leads to greater efficiency and lower costs, which in turn attracts more growth and strengthens our market position.

shows.specific_content: A flywheel diagram illustrating the virtuous cycle of Uber's Freight business. The cycle shows that 'More carriers' leads to an 'Automated network', which enables 'Better carrier utilization' and 'More reliable service'. This results in 'Lower carrier costs' and 'Lower ops costs', leading to a 'Lower shipper price', which drives 'More loads', attracting 'More carriers' and completing the loop. A sidebar provides metrics for 'Marketplace', 'Efficiency', and 'Service' to substantiate the claims.
shows.data_points_shown: Marketplace: 50%+ of loads in bundles, 23% reduction in deadhead miles. Efficiency: 78% of loads auto-tracked. Service: Integration with top 5 TMS players, triple-digit growth in API channel.

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern visualizes a self-reinforcing business model, often called a flywheel or virtuous cycle. It shows how a key input (e.g., more users or suppliers) triggers a series of positive feedback loops, such as improved efficiency, lower costs, or a better product experience. These improvements then attract more of the initial input, causing the cycle to accelerate. It's used to explain the 'how' behind a company's growth and defensibility, demonstrating that growth isn't just linear but compounds over time. The diagram is typically supported by specific metrics that prove each stage of the cycle is working.
works_for: Our marketplace gets better for everyone as it grows: more buyers attract more sellers, which improves selection and lowers prices.
More data from our users allows our AI to create a better product, which in turn attracts more users.
Our growing developer ecosystem builds more apps, making our platform more valuable and attracting more customers.
Increased user engagement generates more content, which drives more traffic from search engines, leading to more user engagement.
As our delivery network densifies, delivery times and costs decrease, which attracts more customers and merchants.
The more people use our payment network, the more merchants accept it, making it more useful for everyone.
Our open-source project's adoption drives enterprise sales, which funds more open-source development.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The core inputs to the cycle (e.g., carriers, users, data, developers).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The outputs and intermediate steps of the cycle (e.g., lower costs, better service, more selection).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Implicit progression; the cycle is shown as a continuous loop that accelerates over time.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Internal logic; the components of the cycle are shown to reinforce each other.

must_have: A clearly defined, multi-step virtuous cycle in the business model
At least one metric to substantiate each key step in the flywheel
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a logical cause-and-effect chain that loops back on itself. The supporting data should show positive trends or high performance for each component.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 3-5 distinct stages in the flywheel, with at least one supporting metric for 2-3 of those stages.

ideal_for: Explaining the core engine of a platform or marketplace business.
Demonstrating a sustainable competitive advantage (moat) that is hard to replicate.
Justifying why the business will become more efficient and profitable as it scales.
Shifting the narrative from linear growth to compounding, accelerating growth.
When pitching a business with strong network effects.
Illustrating how technology creates operational leverage.
avoid_when: Your business model is linear (e.g., a simple services business without network effects).
You cannot provide credible data points to prove the cycle is actually working.
The connections between the steps in your 'flywheel' are weak or purely theoretical.

records.title: Financial model & equity investments

records.core_message: Despite a significant setback from COVID-19, we have taken decisive actions that put us back on track to achieve profitability in the near term and deliver on our ambitious long-term margin targets.

shows.specific_content: A bar chart shows quarterly Adjusted EBITDA margin from Q1'19 to Q4'20, illustrating a pre-COVID improvement, a sharp decline in Q2'20 due to COVID, and a strong recovery. The chart is heavily annotated to explain the trend and projects forward to a 2021 breakeven goal and a 25% long-term target. records.abstract_pattern: This is a 'journey to a target' or 'turnaround' narrative pattern. Any company can use this to show historical progress on a key performance metric, transparently acknowledge a significant setback, and detail the corrective actions taken. The visual then bridges the past performance to a credible future state, defined by specific near-term and long-term targets. This pattern is highly effective for building investor confidence by demonstrating resilience and strategic execution, reframing past negative results as a foundation for future success.
works_for: Our cost-cutting measures have put us on a clear path to positive cash flow next year.
Despite supply chain disruptions, our new manufacturing process will restore gross margins to our 60% target.
